root.note: holy comes from *hailaz ‘whole, healthy’, so holy, whole, heal and health are one family.

stages.meaning: holy day; day of rest and fun
time off work or school, often for travel

history: A holiday was first a holy day. In Old English, hāligdæg meant a religious feast, a day for God. On these days people did not have to work, so by the 1300s the word also meant ‘a day of rest and fun’. Over time the two meanings split. The religious sense stayed with the spelling holy day, and holiday became free time. In British English, holidays are also the long breaks from school and work, and you go on holiday to Spain. Americans say vacation, from Latin vacāre, ‘to be empty, to be free’, and use holiday for public days like Thanksgiving. In the UK, those days are bank holidays.
historyEinfach: Holiday means ‘holy day’. Long ago, a holiday was a day for God. People did not work on these days. So holiday became a word for free time. In the UK, you go on holiday. In the US, people say vacation.

synonyms.note: a short holiday: a weekend break
time off from your job: annual leave

elsewhere.text: German heilig ‘holy’ is a close relative of holy. German heil ‘whole, unhurt’ and heilen ‘to heal’ match English whole and heal. For a day off, German uses Feiertag, from Latin feriae ‘days of rest’.
